Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the redlines you sent earlier. Before we go deep into clause-level negotiation, can we align on sequencing and the immediate operational asks so procurement and legal have a clear handoff? High-level options we see:

- Path A (preferred for speed): Execute MSA + Order Form now; sign an interim DPA referencing the SCCs (EU standard contractual clauses) and a short "transfer addendum" that defers final data location/KMS specifics to a follow-on addendum executed within 60 days.
- Path B (preferred by some customers): Hold signature until DPA is fully finalized with hosting/KMS and subprocessor inventory confirmed.

Questions for you and internal owners:
1) Is MX Health okay with an interim SCCs + transfer-addendum approach (Path A)?
2) Do you require UK Addendum language up front or is EEA SCCs sufficient for now?
3) Any hard procurement deadlines (signed by X date) we should be aware of?

Attached is a short table of outstanding DPA items and owners (MxHealth_DPA_questions.xlsx) and our latest Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v2.pdf) — I highlighted the hosting / KMS callouts.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Please confirm preferred sequencing by EOD Thu 5/28.
- If Path A OK, we propose to circulate a short transfer-addendum template + redlines from our side by Friday.
- If Path B, we will prioritize legal redline calls this week to converge.

Meeting option: 30 minutes tomorrow 10:30am PT if helpful.

Thanks — I want to keep procurement momentum but ensure we don’t bake in a risky data transfer stance.

Best,

Thanks — good summary. Short answers up front:
- Procurement target: signed docs by 6/11. We have an internal board window w/c 6/15 but procurement needs executed docs earlier.
- MX prefers Path A if the interim transfer-addendum explicitly commits to final KMS/hosting region details within 45 days and includes a rollback/fallback if specifics aren’t met.

1) Does Redwood have a standard KMS/Encryption spec we can reference in the interim addendum (we need algos, key custody, and whether customer-managed keys are available)?
2) For training data: will Redwood allow an opt-out for any customer-provided sensitive datasets? We need a line in the DPA that restricts model training on PHI unless explicitly consented.

I’m attaching a narrow redline of the MSA clause we care most about (see attached). Happy to take the short meeting tomorrow at 10:30am PT.

Folks —

Quick engineering/legal POV on sequencing and what we can commit to for Path A:

- Interim transfer-addendum (two-stage approach): OK. We can ship a short addendum that: references EU SCCs, includes UK Addendum language as an annex, and commits to publishing the KMS/location specifics within 45 days of signature. Addendum to include a specific rollback remedy (30-day cure + fall-back to EU-only processing if commitments not met).

- KMS: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS. For the interim addendum we can reference our standard KMS spec: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, HSM-backed CMK options (customer can provide key material via KMS binds). I’ll attach a tech spec (Ben_KMS_specs.pdf).

- Training data: We will add explicit DPA language that prohibits use of customer-provided PHI for model training unless customer provides prior written consent. We suggest the clause: "Customer Data marked as Sensitive Personal Data (defined in Schedule X) will not be used to further train general models without Customer's written opt-in."

- Subprocessor inventory: we can provide a certified list and offer to update it within 7 business days of signature; we won’t make subprocessor changes that increase risk profile for UK/EEA transfers within 30 days without notice (standard notice).

I attached a short redline with suggested sentence-level edits to the transfer addendum (MxHealth_Redwood_transfer_addendum_redline.docx). If Mx wants Path A, legal should sign the short addendum and we can proceed to DocuSign for MSA + Order Form.

Flags for commercial: Markus — path A with CMK and onshore hosting options will impact pricing by ~8–12% depending on region. Need your sign-off for any onshore KMS surcharge.

Ben
